921-program-description: Business basics plus hands-on work in the Retail Innovation Lab: running retail at every level with current technology, consumer behaviour, omni-channel, pricing analytics, payments and global value chains.
921-program-description-2: One of two Strategic Management options. Business in a global setting and its effects on society and the environment: industry structure, competition, organizational capabilities, and different economic and political systems. Leads to consulting, strategic planning in multinationals and government, and business development in start-ups.
922-program-description: Using non-profit, civil and for-profit sectors to tackle social issues. Rethinks strategy around development, environment, responsibility and impact, with cross-sector work and social entrepreneurship, and courses outside the Faculty encouraged. Leads to NGOs, UN-linked bodies, social enterprise, government, consulting and CSR.
922-minors-for-management-students: Arts and Science minors work with any B.Com. unless a department says otherwise; ask a departmental advisor first. Check requirements in a Minerva Degree Evaluation, and return a Minor Approval Form signed by the minor advisor to the office, or the minor may not be granted.
Economics: 18 credits not overlapping Management content, with at most 6 for MGCR 293 and ECON 230D1/D2 or 250D1/D2, and 6 for MGCR 294 or ECON 332 and 333. BCom Office approval needed.
Math, Statistics or Computer Science minors: take MATH 133, 140 and 141 and ask the department.

Statistics: substitute MATH 324 for MGCR 271, counting 3 toward the minor. If you already took MGCR 271, MATH 324 gives 3 more credits, but counts only toward the minor's 18. Check overlaps with the office.
923-minor-in-management-for-non-manageme: 18 credits of managerial skills: required courses plus complementaries. Apply online by the June deadline; decisions come by McGill email in early July. C or better, no S/U. Tell your faculty when approved.
923-entrepreneurship-minors-for-non-mana: 18 credits for Agricultural and Environmental Sciences, Arts, and Education students (Kinesiology and Physical Education; B.A. Education in Global Contexts). Also offered through other faculties: Technological Entrepreneurship for Engineering and Bioresource, Music Entrepreneurship for Schulich, Entrepreneurship for Science.
923-program-description: An entrepreneurial mindset and method, across ventures, social enterprise, start-ups, co-ops, corporate ventures and side projects. Three streams, self-directed and hands-on.
924-agribusiness-stream: 6 credits. FAES 300 counts only if its placement is approved as entrepreneurial.
924-program-description: 18 credits of basic management knowledge for Arts, Engineering, Science, Agricultural and Environmental Sciences, Music, Religious Studies and Kinesiology students.
924-complementary-courses-18-credits: 9 credits from the list. 3 of statistics (MGCR 271 or an approved equivalent); equivalents in statistics or economics from elsewhere don't count, so add another complementary. 9 more from any unused Management courses or 300–400 level ones you qualify for. Check Course Overlap in Arts, Science and Desautels first.
924-management-major-programs: Accounting; Business Analytics; Economics; Finance; Information Technology Management; International Management; Managing for Sustainability; Marketing; Mathematics and Statistics for Management; Organizational Behaviour and Human Resources; Retail Management; Statistics; Strategic Management.
These are demanding, so declare early. Only C or better counts. See the BCom site for mentors.
925-program-description: Preparing, interpreting and using financial and managerial information: financial and managerial accounting, auditing and tax.
925-program-description-2: Interdisciplinary and hands-on, meeting demand for analytics, data science and AI, using modern tools to improve decisions.
926-complementary-courses-18-credits: 3–6 from one list, 6–9 of technical courses, 3–9 from another, or a related topics course approved by the area and B.Com. Office.
926-program-description: A planned sequence in microeconomics and macroeconomics, with options such as econometrics, history, development, environment, industry, trade, labour, money and public finance.
926-complementary-courses-18-credits-2: ECON at 200–400 level, numbered 210 or up. At least 6 at 400-level, at most 6 at 200-level.
927-program-description: 30 credits on top of Core: finance theory, institutions, investment analysis, risk and applied methods. Leads to banking, firms, non-profits and government.
927-program-description-2: Theory, tools and case studies to find business problems, analyze processes and build systems. Covers IT strategy and investment, design and deployment, web businesses, and resistance to change.
928-program-description: 87–90 credits combining business with global study and language skills, on one of three themes: Comparative Global Studies; Global Politics and Economy; Global Well-Being and Development. Includes international business, an outside minor, language courses, and exchange, internship or research.
928-international-business-component: 12 credits. Only one Independent Studies course per B.Com.
929-experiential-learning-component: 0–3 credits: one listed course or an exchange, which has no McGill course; abroad credits count as your adviser decides.
929-research: Only one Independent Studies course per B.Com.
929-international-exchange: Approved courses abroad earn credit and meet this component, with nothing extra. All options have CGPA minimums; see an advisor if you fall short.
929-stream-1-comparative-global-studies: A region (Africa, East Asia, Middle East, South Asia, Europe, the Americas) or a comparison across regions through Religious Studies, Political Science, History or Economics, for work in a region or for global companies or governments. Options include a Minor Concentration in Quebec Studies and Community-Engaged Learning.
Economics: regional ECON courses above 209 (not 295), with 6+ credits at 300–500. MGCR 293 and ECON 295 don't count; neither does ECON 227 if used elsewhere.
929-stream-2-global-politics-and-economy: Public policy through global finance and transactions: war and peace, security, trade, human rights, international organizations. For careers in world and national government, NGOs and global business. Choose Economics, Geography, Political Science or the course group.
930-stream-3-well-being-and-development: Poverty, inequality, health, environment, sustainability and resources, applying business to protect people and the planet.
Economics: ECON courses on environment, development and health above 209 (not 295), with credits at 300–500. MGCR 293 and ECON 295 don't count; neither does ECON 227 if used elsewhere.
930-language-component: 9–12 credits. Either 9 of first- or second-level EAST, or ISLA 221D1/D2; extra Japanese, Chinese or Korean (up to 18) or Arabic count as electives. Don't exceed your degree's total.
Or 12 at 500-level or lower from one subject: CLAS (Modern Greek), EAST (third and fourth level), FREN, FRSL, GERM, HISP, ISLA (Arabic, Turkish, Urdu, Persian), ITAL, JWST (Hebrew, Yiddish), RUSS.

Lower Intermediate Arabic placement means ISLA 322D1/D2 and 423D1/D2 for 12. ITAL 205D1/D2 is for U0 and U1 only; ITAL 206 is for U0–U2; ITAL 210D1/D2, 215D1/D2 and 216 are open. Departments often use placement tests or approval.
931-program-description: Management plus the linked economic, social and ecological challenges of sustainability, with environmental and social science fundamentals, and a real-world consulting project, internship or research.
931-complementary-courses-24-credits: 3–9, 3–9, 0–9 and 6–12 from four lists (or a related topics course approved by the Mentor and BCom Office), plus 3 of environmentally related courses. ENVR courses have limited enrolment.
932-suggested-course-list: Two themes: Social Sciences and Policy; Natural Sciences and Technology. Most 300+ courses have prerequisites. Not exhaustive; others need the Adviser's permission. Courses run on both campuses, so check where.
933-program-description: For many careers, focused on digital marketing, analytics, brands, advertising, innovation and sales.
934-program-description: Newer methods for real-world problems, in 72 or 75 credits.
934-program-prerequisites: 0–10 credits on top of the program, unless already done.
934-complementary-courses-9-12-credits: MGSC 434 counts when relevant and approved by the Mathematics adviser. Check Desautels' statistics sequencing rules.
935-program-description: How people act in groups and organizations: leadership, HR, teams and management levels, plus psychology, sociology, anthropology or industrial relations.
935-complementary-courses-27-credits: 18 from the list and 9 at 300–400 level in PSYC, SOCI, ANTH or INDR with permission. Depth in one is encouraged.
935-program-description-2: AI and automation are changing every stage of retail. Builds analysis, management and communication skills while promoting sustainability. Same admission as other B.Com. programs.
936-program-description: Competition and globalization alongside social and environmental challenges, for large firms, small businesses and social enterprises. Flexible, on top of the Core. Leads to consulting, start-up development and strategy in multinationals, NGOs, international bodies and government.
937-honours-in-investment-management: Honours means more depth, not more volume. Usually register in U1, possibly U2 by arrangement. Normally CGPA and honours average of 3.00, and B- minimum per course; units may set more.
Using MGCR 271 and MGSC 372 (or ECON 227D1/D2) for statistics means taking ECON 468 and 469 in Honours Economics for Management, or Joint Honours in Economics with Accounting or Finance.
937-program-description: Asset management, buy side or sell side: statements, valuation, efficient portfolios, and managing risk with dynamic strategies and derivatives.

Limited, by application, for those entering U2 with a CGPA of 3.3. Graduate with CGPA and program GPA of 3.0, B- or better in all program courses. Otherwise you may still get a Finance Major. On top of Core.
938-quantitative-courses: 6–9 credits. FINE 434 and 435 count with the Academic Director's approval.
938-summer-studies-in-management: Make up gaps or speed up, early May to July, for Management and qualified others. Offerings vary by year. Limit: 6 credits per summer, unless the office agrees. Contact advisors or Service Point, 514-398-7878, summer.studies@mcgill.ca, mcgill.ca/summer.

Elsewhere: apply for Independent Study Away in Minerva and get equivalency and transfer forms approved before the course starts; no overlaps. Residency and online limits apply. Finish in summer, with transcripts in by September 15. Cancel in writing if you don't register. No McGill courses at the same time. Short programs usually need an exchange partner. Complete the Travel Registry.
IUT follows the same rules and needs early approval, without guaranteeing a seat.
940-about-the-faculty-of-medicine-and-he: McGill's first faculty and Canada's first medical faculty, founded in 1829, known for biomedical science, epigenetics, neuroscience, stem cells and regenerative medicine. Six schools: Biomedical Sciences, Communication Sciences and Disorders, Medicine, Nursing, Physical and Occupational Therapy, and Population and Global Health.
940-mission-and-values: Combining science and humanism to train health professionals and scientists for Quebec and the world. Values: altruism, humanism, collaboration, creativity and rigour.
940-outstanding-education-for-outstandin: Over 8,000 students, residents and fellows; over 5,000 academics and 900 support staff; focused on education, research and service, with advanced experiential facilities.
940-collaborative-research-and-care-for-: Over 60% of McGill's research. Supports training on how health and disease work, ambitious problem-driven research, interdisciplinary work, and moving knowledge into care.
940-delivering-with-and-for-communities: Works for openness, belonging and respect among its people, and engages communities on unmet needs through partnerships, outreach and advocacy.
